issues.expected: The collision avoidance system composite is reachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.observed: CollisionAvoidanceSystem is unreachable from the top-level initial entry.
issues.reason: The required collision-avoidance scope is an independently initialized operating composite, but the finite closed-model reachability facts show that CollisionAvoidanceSystem is not reached from the top-level initial entry.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The collision-avoidance composite is declared and contains its required states, but declaration and containment do not establish root reachability; no supplied top-level entry reaches it.

issues.basis: NL12 source identity, exact owner and target bindings, transition:line:71 targeting state:UnspecifiedInitial:line:70, and inspection initial-entry facts.
issues.expected: The CollisionAvoidanceSystem owner-local initial edge enters collision_avoidance_deactive.
issues.observed: The owner-local initial edge transition:line:71 enters UnspecifiedInitial instead.
issues.reason: The exact owner-local initial edge for CollisionAvoidanceSystem targets the synthetic UnspecifiedInitial state. No owner-local edge targets collision_avoidance_deactive, so the required default entry is not realized.
issues.requirement_quote: The collision avoidance system is initially in the collision_avoidance_deactive state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The required inactive state exists and has the required activation transition, but it is not the target of the exact owner-local initial edge; the nearby synthetic entry cannot satisfy the scoped requirement.

issues.basis: NL3 group ALT-NL3-CRUISE and ALT-NL3-LANE-CHANGE, exact transitions transition:line:24 and transition:line:25, and the absence of a supplied finite guard domain.
issues.expected: The exclusive enter_hwy alternatives have distinguishable conditions.
issues.observed: Both alternatives use the same effective trigger condition.
issues.reason: Both exact enter_hwy alternatives carry the same effective trigger, dist_to_front<25 and extra_lane=true, so the closed transition group provides no supplied condition that distinguishes cruise from lane_change.
issues.requirement_quote: In the HighwayMode state, the system begins in the enter_hwy substate, and can transition to cruise or lane_change based on the distance to the front vehicle (`dist_to_front<25`) and the availability of an extra lane (`extra_lane=true`).
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The source wording can be read as permitting both destinations under one compound condition; without an independently supplied domain or exclusivity rule, frozen guard-disjointness execution cannot decide the semantic collision.
issues.title: Shared condition does not distinguish enter_hwy alternatives

issues.basis: Derived NL1 endpoint contract; source transition tr_0002; complete closed transition inventory shows transition:line:63 has source [*] and target InitialState, while no AutonomousMode-to-InitialState state transition exists.
issues.expected: A direct transition from AutonomousMode to InitialState exists.
issues.observed: No direct AutonomousMode-to-InitialState transition exists; the closed model instead has an owner-local initial pseudostate edge to InitialState.
issues.reason: The source-derived endpoint contract treats AutonomousMode to InitialState as a direct transition. The closed transition inventory has no direct state-to-state edge with those endpoints; the available edge is an initial-pseudostate edge inside AutonomousMode, so the exact endpoint pair is absent under the derived transition property.
issues.requirement_quote: The system begins in the AutonomousMode state, which transitions into the InitialState substate, marking the starting point of the autonomous driving mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: In hierarchical state-machine semantics, an owner-local initial pseudostate edge can implement the source-level phrase that AutonomousMode transitions into InitialState; the direct endpoint contract is therefore dependent on whether the derived contract's direct-edge interpretation is accepted.
issues.title: AutonomousMode-to-InitialState Endpoint Is Absent As A Direct Edge

issues.basis: NL12 derived event-consumer contract; source transition tr_0024; closed transition:line:72 and state:collision_avoidance_deactive:line:68; event-consumer and finite verification facts show a declared consumer with an empty reachable consumer set.
issues.expected: The collision avoidance danger stimuli are consumed by a reachable inactive-to-active transition within the collision avoidance system.
issues.observed: The consumer transition exists and is declared, but reachable_consumer_transition_refs is empty and the inactive state is unreachable.
issues.reason: The exact inactive-to-active consumer exists and is declared, but its consumer state and transition are unreachable from any top-level initial entry. This is a distinct operational consumer-coverage property, not a claim that the endpoint transition is absent.
issues.requirement_quote: It transitions to collision_avoidance_active when certain conditions are met, such as detecting pedestrians (`pedestrian_detected`), the rear distance being less than 5 meters with a velocity over 30 km/h (`dist_to_rear<5 & vel>30`), or the front distance being less than 15 meters in highway mode or 10 meters in urban mode.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The transition and its event projection are present, and the source does not explicitly state top-level reachability; the issue concerns operational coverage inferred from the required collision-avoidance behavior and the supplied deterministic reachable-consumer fact.
issues.title: Collision Danger Consumer Is Unreachable
